=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:275-296 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The fingerprint-cap gate prefers the self-repository PR-head copy of `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py`, allowing a PR to influence the helper result used to decide whether its review is capped.
  WHY: The gate validates output shape but not helper provenance, so a modified helper could return a valid-looking count and falsify the cap decision; the blast radius is narrow because other review paths remain.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:847 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The gate loop searches `.codex-workflow-src/scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py` before `.codex-workflow-src-main/scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py`, allowing a self-repository PR to influence identical-failure counting.
  WHY: The gate trusts the untrusted helper output, which could under-count or over-count failures and suppress review or waste reviewer budget.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:700-732 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: `derive_autofix_failure_reason` does not map `EDITOR_NOOP_RECOVERABLE_FAILURE` or `EDITOR_NOOP_SUSPICIOUS` to dedicated reason tokens.
  WHY: Those branches fall through to `finalize_reason` or `workflow_failure`, so operators cannot distinguish them from generic failures through the reason field; the fingerprint counting itself remains differentiated where stated.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:1826-1859 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When `extract_repo_scoped_issue_refs_from_text` is unavailable in an older staged `label_helpers.sh`, the cap-block job labels only the PR and does not propagate `ai:review-blocked` to linked issues.
  WHY: Managed issues can remain labelled `ai:implementing` or `ai:planning`, delaying or preventing issue-level stall recovery and wave-completion handling.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:780-800 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The paired-summary scan uses a single-use `skip_paired_summary` boolean, so a second editor summary in the relevant marker sequence is treated as a success marker and terminates the scan.
  WHY: The identical-failure count can be undercounted by one and delay cap activation; one review notes that the triggering comment ordering has no natural runtime path.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:1684-1916 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Concurrent runs can both observe `FINGERPRINT_CAP_ALREADY_APPLIED=false` before either cap-block job posts its marker, producing duplicate cap comments and duplicate `identical_failure_cap` heal reports.
  WHY: Label writes are idempotent but comments and dispatches are not; reviewers note that the existing concurrency and dispatch guards make this a narrow race.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:616-618 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The `gate_fetch_marker_comments` jq expression broadly matches substrings such as `"AI review/autofix"` and `"review-autofix-failure"`, including quoted mentions in unrelated comments.
  WHY: Such comments can increase the fetched comment set and may risk incorrect scan behavior; one review notes that trusted-author and exact-marker filtering makes the broader pre-fetch harmless.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:1772-1777 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: If the cap-block PR fetch fails and writes `{}`, the empty `current_head` bypasses the head-moved check and the job proceeds with stale gate data.
  WHY: The job can label the PR without verifying that the gate evaluated the current PR head.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:1894-1902 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The cap-block heal reporter receives a `REPORT_SUMMARY_LINE_FILE` path that does not exist.
  WHY: `FINALIZE_REASON` remains empty, although `AUTOFIX_FAILURE_REASON="identical_failure_cap"` takes precedence and makes the missing file harmless in the current path.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:1718-1750 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: Both fingerprint-cap-block checkout steps use `continue-on-error: true`, so missing support files trigger less robust inline fallback helpers.
  WHY: The fail-open path can silently fail individual label or comment writes because the inline helpers lack the canonical retry, error handling, and Telegram integration.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
(No task gaps reported.)
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml: Gate job, fingerprint cap helper check — the gate loop at line ~847 searches `.codex-workflow-src/scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py` first (the support-ref copy, which in self-repo equals `github.sha` = the PR's own head), before `.codex-workflow-src-main/scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py` (main snapshot) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A self-repo PR modifying workflow_failure_heal.py could have the gate use its own untrusted copy to falsify the identical-failure count, potentially suppressing review by under-counting or over-counting.
  WHY: The gate trusts the output of the untrusted helper; the attack requires commit access and independently validated numeric output.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:714-732, derive_autofix_failure_reason | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The function only maps AUTOFIX_EDITOR_EMPTY_NOOP, EDITOR_CHANGES_LOST, and EDITOR_NOOP_REFUSAL to explicit reason tokens.
  WHY: EDITOR_NOOP_RECOVERABLE_FAILURE and EDITOR_NOOP_SUSPICIOUS fall through to finalize_reason or workflow_failure, producing less specific fingerprints and operator-visible reasons.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:1826-1830, cap-block job, extract_repo_scoped_issue_refs_from_text fallback | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When the function is unavailable, linked issues are silently omitted and only the PR is labeled.
  WHY: Per-issue label propagation is lost and issue-level stall recovery is delayed until the poller's next wave-status sweep.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:170-176, 873-877, count_identical_failures paired-summary loop | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: After skip_paired_summary resets to False at line 876, a second editor summary appearing between the same pair of failure markers is treated as a normal success marker and breaks the scan.
  WHY: The count would be exactly one lower, although the comment ordering does not arise naturally because each run posts one summary and one failure comment.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:1687-1913, fingerprint-cap-block job | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Two concurrent workflow_dispatch runs could both pass the gate and produce duplicate cap comments and duplicate heal reports.
  WHY: The workflow carries a concurrency group that serializes runs on the same PR branch under normal GitHub scheduling, so this path requires removal or failure of that enforcement.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:616-618, gate_fetch_marker_comments jq filter | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The contains("AI review/autofix") filter selects any comment quoting the phrase, including non-failure comments from reviewers who quote the cap-block comment.
  WHY: Trusted-author filtering excludes reviewer comments from the count; the broad filter only increases stored comment volume.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:1894-1902, cap-block job heal reporter invocation, REPORT_SUMMARY_LINE_FILE="${work_dir}/no_summary_line.txt" | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The reporter is passed a reference to a file that does not exist.
  WHY: FINALIZE_REASON stays empty, but AUTOFIX_FAILURE_REASON="identical_failure_cap" takes precedence and the missing file is harmless.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:1718-1750, fingerprint-cap-block checkout steps | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Both checkout steps carry continue-on-error: true, causing fallback to less robust inline helpers when support files are unavailable.
  WHY: The fail-open path still labels and posts the cap comment, but individual label or comment writes can silently fail.

=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:gate_fetch_marker_comments function, jq expression | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The jq expression filters comments by broad substrings like "AI review/autofix" and "review-autofix-failure".
  WHY: Quoted mentions in unrelated comments may be captured and cause the failure scan to terminate prematurely or misidentify markers.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:derive_autofix_failure_reason function | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The derivation logic does not explicitly handle EDITOR_NOOP_RECOVERABLE_FAILURE or EDITOR_NOOP_SUSPICIOUS as reason tokens.
  WHY: Those branches fall back to workflow_failure or finalize_reason, preventing operators from identifying recoverable or no-op-suspicious issues through the reason field.

=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:derive_autofix_failure_reason (introduced in fingerprint-cap diff; around the new function block at lines 700-715) | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: derive_autofix_failure_reason only recognises AUTOFIX_EDITOR_EMPTY_NOOP, EDITOR_CHANGES_LOST, and EDITOR_NOOP_REFUSAL.
  WHY: The two failure branches in review_autofix.yml that gate on EDITOR_NOOP_RECOVERABLE_FAILURE and EDITOR_NOOP_SUSPICIOUS never reach a dedicated token.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:fingerprint-cap-block job, Apply identical-failure cap outcome step (cap-marker / linked-issue labelling block ~review_autofix.yml:1834-1859) | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When extract_repo_scoped_issue_refs_from_text is unavailable from the staged label_helpers.sh, the job warns and falls through to label only the PR.
  WHY: A consumer repo whose staged label_helpers.sh predates the function misses every linked issue on every cap-block run, so the issue stays labelled ai:implementing / ai:planning while the PR itself is labelled ai:review-blocked.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:fingerprint-cap-block job (lines ~1684-1907), specifically the FINGERPRINT_CAP_ALREADY_APPLIED check at the top of the "Apply identical-failure cap outcome" step | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Two concurrent workflow_dispatch runs on the same head can both observe FINGERPRINT_CAP_ALREADY_APPLIED=false and both proceed to post cap comments and dispatch heal reports.
  WHY: Labels are idempotent, but comments and dispatch reports are not; existing concurrency guards make the race narrow.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:count_identical_failures, paired-summary loop (around the new function at lines 780-800) | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: skip_paired_summary is a single-use boolean, so two editor summaries in the relevant sequence can cause the second summary to terminate the scan before the following failure marker.
  WHY: The cap count can be undercounted by one and trip one run later than intended.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:gate's fingerprint-cap block, head-moved short-circuit (around review_autofix.yml:1772-1777 inside the fingerprint-cap-block job) | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: A
